title: Decision-critical questions
rule: A question is answered only when an official source settles it and that source is linked. The P0/P1/P2 priority is about what unblocks the most work per unit of effort, not urgency.

questions.question: Is a five-club depth pilot an acceptable evidence base, or should the site publish the 31-club join that already exists?
questions.known: 31 of 32 clubs already have a club-depth-chart collection in the repository (1803 entries, every row linked to its club page).
questions.missing: A decision on whether a club self-report counts as evidence, and what to do about the one club (HOU) with no parsable chart.
questions.closes_with: A one-line owner ruling recorded in COORDINATION.md.
questions.recommend: Publish the full join and label every row 'club self-report', keeping the pilot visible as a subset.
questions.there_after: The injury page can state a real count of exposed starters instead of a floor.
questions.source_note: illustrates the problem: the page footer prints 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'

questions.blocks: Every ROI, edge and leaderboard figure
questions.question: Which line is the benchmark: one book's closing line, a consensus, or a market-weighted average?
questions.known: Three different references are in use across the four trees; the research lab names and fingerprints its source.
questions.missing: A named provider with terms, and a rule for which snapshot of the line counts.
questions.closes_with: A written benchmark definition, or a licensed feed.
questions.recommend: Pick one and make it a field on every result row; the repository already fingerprints its current source.
questions.there_after: Results from the four trees become comparable, and the leaderboard becomes meaningful.
questions.source_note: documents the mirror; it does not name the original book

questions.question: What counts as a starter when no league-published depth chart exists?
questions.known: The league publishes no depth chart; clubs publish their own and label them unofficial.
questions.missing: A reproducible rule that survives a club changing its chart mid-week.
questions.closes_with: A definition written down before the next chart is collected.
questions.recommend: Use 'first listed at his position slot on his own club's chart on the retrieval date' — it is mechanical and auditable, which is what the join already does.
questions.there_after: Depth claims become re-runnable and citable.

questions.question: What are the actual reward rules, and is paying them lawful where the owner lives?
questions.known: The gates define who is eligible; the reward formula is specified.
questions.missing: Funding, payout mechanics, and the legal position in the owner's jurisdiction.
questions.closes_with: A written rule set plus local legal advice.
questions.recommend: Run the competition with a paper ledger first; no money changes hands until the rules are legal and written.
questions.there_after: The leaderboard can reward skill without creating a liability.
questions.source_note: the league operates the game, not the contest; reward rules are an owner decision

questions.question: Where do prop prices and player participation data come from, given no market prop feed is reachable?
questions.known: A prop model and its calibration exist; no prop price exists anywhere in the repository.
questions.missing: A licensed prop feed and snap counts.
questions.closes_with: A vendor, or an explicit decision to keep props off the leaderboard.
questions.recommend: Keep props as published mathematics only — the model, the calibration and the break-even arithmetic — and say so.
questions.there_after: Prop work stops looking like an unrun strategy and starts being a documented method.
questions.source_note: league player stats are published; prop prices are not

questions.blocks: Judging whether any strategy is real
questions.question: How do we know a strategy's edge is not simply a shared blind spot between our two transcriptions?
questions.known: Two independent transcriptions agree on every compared value; one strategy passes all eight gates out of sample.
questions.missing: A third independent source for the line values themselves, or the raw league feed.
questions.closes_with: A second price source, or a documented decision that the mirror is acceptable.
questions.recommend: Treat agreement as evidence of correct transcription, not of a correct benchmark — flag F-13 already says this; keep it visible next to the result.
questions.there_after: The passing strategy is understood as conditional on the benchmark, not established as profitable.
questions.source_note: community mirror, not a league feed

questions.question: What should the site do when the official page changes after publication?
questions.known: The injury report changes daily; the published tables are dated snapshots.
questions.missing: A rule for superseding a published row, and whether the old value is kept.
questions.recommend: Keep every snapshot, publish the retrieval timestamp per row, and never overwrite a published value in place.
questions.there_after: A decision made in Week 12 can still cite what was true in Week 10.
questions.source_note: the league's own page changes and publishes no archive of prior states
